To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Coulomb-modified GCM is able to describe reaction cross sections for a variety of heavy-ion systems over a wide energy range, including the Coulomb barrier region, and that the Coulomb field is the main reason for the discrepancy between the GCM and the data for heavy-ion systems with Z1Z2 > 400.
the reaction cross sections of heavy ions can be well described in the framework of the modified Glauber model with Coulomb field correction.

(a) we have obtained a closed-form analytic expression, within the framework of Glauber model, for the reaction cross sections for heavy-ion systems involving Coulomb field effect; (b) we have obtained the Coulomb-modified GSI parameterization of the nucleon-nuclon cross section, and (c) we have obtained an expression for the reaction cross section of the heavy-ion systems, which is valid over the entire energy range beginning with Coulomb barrier to few GeV/n
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of heavy ion reactions in the intermediate energy range (20–200 MeV/u), where both the nuclear and the Coulomb interactions play an important role.
the study of the reaction cross section for heavy-ion systems in the energy range from the Coulomb barrier up to a few GeVs per nucleon.
the development of a theoretical description of heavy-ion reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Coulomb-modified GCM is a useful model to describe heavy-ion reaction cross-sections in the energy range of 1 to 1000 MeV/nucleon.
the Coulomb-modified GCM is an accurate, reliable, and convenient tool for the prediction of heavy-ion reaction data.
the Glauber-Coulomb model provides a simple, accurate, and useful description of heavy-ion cross sections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Glauber theory is capable of describing the reaction cross sections for all heavy-ion systems, including light, medium and heavy, at energies above the Coulomb barrier.
the Coulomb effect is important in heavy-ion reaction cross-section calculations, but the nuclear effect is dominant.
the Glauber theory is a good approximation to the reaction cross section for heavy ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Coulomb field has a significant effect on the reaction cross section.
the reaction cross section for heavy-ion collisions is a function of two parameters: the nucleon-nuclon cross section and the nuclear density profile of the projectile and target.
the Coulomb field has a profound impact on the reaction cross section, especially in the intermediate energy range.
